title: Thor v249 - the phone keyboard layouts go into the system volume at boot

candidate_change: The keyboard: the phone layouts of the same build go into the system volume. The iPad restore carries KBLayouts_iPad.dat and no KBLayouts_iPhone.dat, and UIKit on the phone persona asks for a phone layout, so the keyboard never appeared. From the iPhone XR restore of 18.7.10 / 22H374 every resource of TextInputUI, TextInput, TextInputCore and KeyboardServices is added to the same frameworks of the guest (upstream's fix of services112, userland/phone_components18.py; here thor/phone_resources.py): 8 files, 3255032 bytes, 7 of them replacing an iPad file, KBLayouts_iPad.dat kept. The Phone application, the telephone bundles and the carrier bundles are not in this image.

How it reaches the phone: the system volume (the OS window of SHNGROOT, mounted read-only) was changed in a copy of the installed window on the Mac. The 925 blocks of 4096 bytes that differ (3788800 bytes in 66 runs: 920 data blocks, the newest container superblock, 4 other superblocks) travel as one file in the boot image's FAT volume (/efi/unixnu/os-patch.bin, 3911680 bytes; thor/os_patch.py), and the device tree names its place in boot_a (/chosen thor-os-patch-offset and thor-os-patch-bytes). Before the storage transport publishes any window the kernel streams the file from boot_a, a partition of the firmware LUN, and applies it: nothing is written unless every record is, on the phone, exactly the original or already the new content; the data blocks go first and the newest superblock last; every block is read back (bsd/kern/thor_os_patch.h, called from drivers/NativeUfs/PongUfsTransport.cpp; the read of boot_a is bounded to the file's own blocks in RootCommands.h). On a later boot every record is already new and nothing is written; a patch cut off at any point is continued by the next boot. The same code was run on the Mac against image files: applied, applied again, refused when a block or the first blocks differ, resumed after interruptions and torn writes. Not run on the phone at the time of writing.

Carried unchanged from v248: the first page of a panic names the fault; the camera inventory does not start (/chosen has no thor-camera); every death by a signal is recorded (PONG DEATH); the log capture library v247 in eight processes; the display library of v246; the UI adapter in PosterBoard; the Wi-Fi station's retries (Wi-Fi joined on v247, reported by the user).  No boot argument changed; the device tree is v248's plus the two /chosen properties that name the OS patch's place in boot_a.

config_change.device_tree_changed: v248's plus /chosen thor-os-patch-offset and thor-os-patch-bytes (where the image keeps the OS patch in boot_a); no /chosen thor-camera (the camera inventory of v247 does not start); the root node wlan is kept
config_change.wifid_start: launchd starts wifid at boot; a library in it waits until configd has published the marker and listed en0 and a power source is on the registry (or 150 s), then wifid runs; killed and started again when it has not asked the driver within 60 s

manifest.diagnostic_delta: new: PONG_UFS OS PATCH V249 lines before the windows are published (the firmware LUN answers, or why the patch was not applied) and THOR OS PATCH V249 lines (the records verified, written and read back). Unchanged: THOR PANIC V248 lines on the first page of a panic; PONG DEATH lines; libpong-logcap-v247.dylib in eight processes; libpong-display-v246.dylib in backboardd; the signed UI adapter in PosterBoard; libpong-wifid-v244.dylib in wifid; libpong-probe-v244.dylib in PosterBoard, configd and wifid; Settings diagnostic as v238; console capture as v232
